clue.text: Complete diplomat excels thus

definitions.meaning: a good diplomat excels ..., so the phrase read as two words describes how a diplomat shines

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works only when the answer is split into two words: a diplomat excels IN TACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something complete has nothing missing or broken.

clue.text: Scott's hero in Russian garden

parts.note: Ivan is the stock Russian man's name, used for a typical Russian
to hoe is to work a garden with a hoe

explanation.surface: Sir Walter Scott's hero is pictured relaxing in a garden in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Title character: Sir Walter Scott's novel is named after its knightly protagonist, Wilfred of Ivanhoe.

clue.text: Stare goofily, seeing stunner

indicators.note: doing something goofily means doing it in a daft, disordered way, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone gawps foolishly on seeing a stunningly attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' looks like a beautiful person; here it is a device that stuns.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: the device delivers an electric shock that stuns its target.

clue.text: Order arms, for example, for the military

definitions.text: Order arms, for example, for the military

parts.words: Order arms, for example, for the military
parts.note: 'Order arms' is a drill instruction shouted on the parade ground, an example of the kind of instruction soldiers obey

explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like the definition alone, but the clue is one cryptic description: 'Order arms' is itself a military drill instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a parade-ground drill instruction is an authoritative directive given to soldiers.

clue.text: A rolling sea, too

parts.note: a swell is the long rolling motion of the sea

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the sea is rough as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both phrases mean in addition or also.

clue.text: Careless and sentimental about love, primarily

indicators.note: about means going round, so the sentimental word wraps around the letter

parts.note: soppy means mawkishly sentimental

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letter of the word love is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is described as both careless and mushy about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careless and sentimental' looks like a single two-part definition, but 'sentimental' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: slapdash, untidy work done without care.

clue.text: Very enthusiastic e-bulletin put out

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed or upset, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: An electronic newsletter has been issued in an excited tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as published, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: full of cheerful energy and excitement.

clue.text: Scientist's garment of short, dense hair?

definitions.meaning: the white overall worn in a laboratory
a Labrador dog has short, thick fur, its coat; the question mark admits the play on lab for Labrador

explanation.walkthrough: LAB is short for laboratory and for Labrador, a dog with short, dense fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: the white protective overall worn in a laboratory.

clue.text: Power behind the throne terrible in emergencies

indicators.note: terrible suggests something badly wrecked, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shadowy adviser to the monarch performs badly in crises.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: French for 'grey eminence', a hidden adviser who wields influence without the formal title.

clue.text: My father's son? I don't know

parts.note: Pa is father, so possessive Pa's

explanation.surface: A puzzled person asks whose son they are and admits ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiz convention: a contestant who cannot answer says this word to move on.

clue.text: A rhyme for elephant? That's incomprehensible

definitions.meaning: Jumbo is a pet name for an elephant, and the word in front rhymes with it
a term for gibberish or nonsense meant to confuse

explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo was a famous London Zoo elephant, so the name stands for any elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: meaningless jargon or ritual that baffles the listener.

clue.text: Part of opera needs quiet first — it's the law

indicators.note: first places the quiet letters before the operatic part

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an aria is a solo song within an opera

explanation.surface: A section of an opera demands silence before it begins, by legal requirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific instance: Islamic religious law derived from the Koran and the Prophet's teaching.

clue.text: No French can admit another European as emperor

indicators.note: admit means let in, so the French word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: non is French for no
since the French speaker is already European, another one is a Pole

explanation.surface: France refuses entry to a fellow European who would be emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: Asking is difficult

definitions.meaning: requesting firmly, as in calling for something
hard, taxing, as a tough job is

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: present participle of a verb for requesting, and an adjective for hard work.

clue.text: Target a friend of the family?

definitions.meaning: an object of easy criticism, from a fairground game of throwing at a dummy
split differently, the answer is an ..., someone friendly to a relative

explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally was a British fairground dummy at which balls were thrown; the name now means an easy target. Split as AUNT'S ALLY, it is a friend of a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: someone or something set up to be criticised or attacked.

clue.text: Flat rate?

parts.note: a flat rate usually means a fixed charge, but here it is what one pays to live in an apartment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat rate' looks like a fixed fee; read literally it is the charge for a flat, British for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal reading: the regular payment a tenant makes for an apartment.

clue.text: One with obsessive interest about fish

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: a nut is a fanatic, someone obsessed with a hobby

explanation.surface: An enthusiast is obsessed with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of the phrase 'interest about'; it signals that A NUT is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large oily sea fish, often canned.

clue.text: Suffered possibly painful eruption, by gum!

definitions.text: Suffered possibly painful eruption, by gum!

parts.words: Suffered possibly painful eruption, by gum!
parts.note: by gum is an old exclamation, but literally it means through the gums, where a baby's new teeth break out

explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum!' reads as a Northern English exclamation; literally it is where the eruption happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: a baby's first teeth erupt through the gums, often sorely.

clue.text: Take back on board

parts.note: seize again, as a ship's crew might regain control on board, or a chess player regain a piece on the board

explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests accepting an idea; it may instead point to retaking a captured ship or a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to seize again something that had been lost.

clue.text: Haughtily, ladies entering a horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the toilet word goes into the other pieces

parts.note: a fly was a light one-horse hired carriage
the ladies is a women's toilet, and loo is British slang for toilet

explanation.surface: Women climb snootily into a carriage pulled by a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A fly is an old one-horse carriage for hire.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in a distant, standoffish manner.

clue.text: Regularly drew beer up and feasted

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
regularly means every other letter of the word drew is taken

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone poured beer at regular intervals while others enjoyed a feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes D and E from 'drew'; with LAGER that gives DELAGER, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: entertained lavishly with food and drink.

clue.text: Heavens! The French abuse a speaker

parts.note: heck is a mild exclamation of surprise like heavens
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French audience member shouts in dismay at a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym phrase: to interrupt and jeer at someone making a public speech.

clue.text: Suits people to curse

parts.note: men are people
to swear is to curse

explanation.surface: Something is suitable for people who like to swear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' looks like a verb meaning pleases; it is the noun, clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: men's suits are a type of clothing for males.

clue.text: Fruit in old kitchen area

parts.note: a range is a kitchen cooking stove

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit sits in an old-fashioned kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a round citrus fruit.

clue.text: Particular smell in Emilia-Romagna

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the region's name

explanation.surface: A distinctive scent is noticed in an Italian region.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a distinctive, usually pleasant scent.

clue.text: People such as this feel OK, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected turn, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some people are pleasantly surprised to feel all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a phrase meaning persons of a given type.

clue.text: First off, makes dirty picture

definitions.note: the definition is singular while the answer is plural, which the blog queried

indicators.note: first off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: soils means makes dirty

explanation.surface: First of all, an artwork corrupts its viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First off' reads as an opening phrase but signals removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonymy: paintings done in oil paint, as in an exhibition of these.

clue.text: Dead, by collapsing here in hospital?

indicators.note: collapsing means falling apart, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient collapses dead beside a bed in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bed used during the day for patients not staying overnight.

clue.text: Purchase bananas, we hear, but not automatically

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is spoken aloud, giving a similar sound

parts.note: to buy is to purchase, and a hand is a bunch of bananas

explanation.surface: Shoppers buy bananas in person rather than by machine.
explanation.walkthrough: A hand is a cluster of bananas growing together on a stem.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: done manually rather than by a machine.
